# Exploration

Make relationships understandable through the person's own actions.

Give the person a meaningful starting state and a small set of controls that correspond to choices they understand. Keep inputs and their consequences visible together. Make a change produce clear feedback while preserving the context needed to compare it with what came before.

Show what the result means, what assumptions shape it, and where its limits matter. Make reset and comparison easy to discover. An unfamiliar relationship can begin with a revealing example; the person can then vary it, inspect the result, and pursue their own question.
